$$

$$

 

Letting $\theta =\frac{x}{6},$ we get

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{1}{2}\operatorname{sin}⁡(\frac{x}{3}) & =\operatorname{sin}⁡(\frac{x}{6})\operatorname{cos}⁡(\frac{x}{6}).\end{aligned}
$$

Substituting this into our integral, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}{\int }_{0}^{3\pi /2}\operatorname{sin}⁡(\frac{x}{6})\operatorname{cos}⁡(\frac{x}{6})\text{d}x & ={\int }_{0}^{3\pi /2}\frac{1}{2}\operatorname{sin}⁡(\frac{x}{3})\text{d}x \\  & =\frac{1}{2}{\int }_{0}^{3\pi /2}\operatorname{sin}⁡(\frac{x}{3})\text{d}x \\  & =\frac{1}{2}[-3\operatorname{cos}⁡(\frac{x}{3})]{|}_{0}^{3\pi /2} \\  & =-\frac{3}{2}\operatorname{cos}⁡(\frac{x}{3})\,{|}_{0}^{3\pi /2} \\  & =-\frac{3}{2}[\operatorname{cos}⁡(\frac{\pi }{2})-\operatorname{cos}⁡(0)] \\  & =-\frac{3}{2}[0-1] \\  & =\frac{3}{2}.\end{aligned}

Find the area $A$ of the region in the $xy$-plane that is bounded by the curve $y=4{cos}^{2}⁡(2x)+{sin}^{2}⁡(2x),$ the $x$-axis and the lines $x=0$ and $x=\frac{\pi }{4},$ as shown above. Do not round the answer

$A=$
{{field-1}}" :question/worked-solution "The area of the region is given by

$$
A={\int }_{0}^{\pi /4}(4{cos}^{2}⁡(2x)+{sin}^{2}⁡(2x))\,\text{d}x.
$$

Recall  ${cos}^{2}⁡x+{sin}^{2}⁡x=1,$ so we have 

$$
\begin{aligned}4{cos}^{2}⁡(2x)+{sin}^{2}⁡(2x) & =3{cos}^{2}⁡(2x)+({sin}^{2}⁡(2x)+{cos}^{2}⁡(2x)) \\  & =3{cos}^{2}⁡(2x)+1.\end{aligned}
$$

Here, we use the double-angle formula for cosine that involves the ${cos}^{2}⁡x$ term, given by

$$
\operatorname{cos}⁡2x=2{cos}^{2}⁡x-1.
$$

 

Rearranging, we have

$$
2{cos}^{2}⁡x=\operatorname{cos}⁡2x+1.
$$

Hence, the area of the region is

$$
\begin{aligned}A & ={\int }_{0}^{\pi /4}(3{cos}^{2}⁡(2x)+1)\,\text{d}x \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{\pi /4}(\frac{3}{2}\operatorname{cos}⁡4x+\frac{3}{2}+1)\,\text{d}x \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{\pi /4}(\frac{3}{2}\operatorname{cos}⁡4x+\frac{5}{2})\,\text{d}x \\  & ={(\frac{3}{8}\operatorname{sin}⁡4x+\frac{5}{2}x)|}_{0}^{\pi /4} \\  & =[\frac{3}{8}\operatorname{sin}⁡(4\cdot \frac{\pi }{4})+\frac{5}{2}\cdot \frac{\pi }{4}]-[\frac{3}{8}\operatorname{sin}⁡(4\cdot 0)+\frac{5}{2}\cdot 0] \\  & =[\frac{3}{8}\operatorname{sin}⁡(\pi )+\frac{5\pi }{8}]-[\frac{3}{8}\operatorname{sin}⁡(0)+0] \\  & =[\frac{3}{8}\cdot 0+\frac{5\pi }{8}]-[\frac{3}{8}\cdot 0+0] \\  & =\frac{5\pi }{8}.\end{aligned}
$$" :question/difficulty :question.difficulty/hard :question/answer-fields ["answer-field-5275b8a3-a8ed-51bd-8426-91952cbec909"] :db/ensure [:question/validate]} {:db/id "answer-field-5275b8a3-a8ed-51bd-8426-91952cbec909" :answer-field/id #uuid "5275b8a3-a8ed-51bd-8426-91952cbec909" :answer-field/key "field-1" :answer-field/type :answer-field.type/blank :answer-field/correct "answer-8c2da0af-70e4-5430-8430-baeb3a4118a8" :answer-field/choices ["answer-8c2da0af-70e4-5430-8430-baeb3a4118a8"] :db/ensure [:answer-field/validate]} {:db/id "answer-8c2da0af-70e4-5430-8430-baeb3a4118a8" :answer/id #uuid "8c2da0af-70e4-5430-8430-baeb3a4118a8" :answer/type :answer.type/math :answer/value "\frac{5\pi}{8}" :db/ensure [:answer/validate]} {:db/id 17592186318511 :answer-field/correct "answer-1e4f061a-ff83-54a7-966d-5615c8fefe75" :answer-field/choices ["answer-1e4f061a-ff83-54a7-966d-5615c8fefe75"] :db/ensure [:answer-field/validate]} {:db/id "answer-1e4f061a-ff83-54a7-966d-5615c8fefe75" :answer/id #uuid "1e4f061a-ff83-54a7-966d-5615c8fefe75" :answer/type :answer.type/math :answer/value "3\pi" :db/ensure [:answer/validate]} {:db/id 17592186318549 :answer-field/correct "answer-140301e9-e5d7-5ea2-aa4c-0f869d4dbf85" :answer-field/choices ["answer-140301e9-e5d7-5ea2-aa4c-0f869d4dbf85"] :db/ensure [:answer-field/validate]} {:db/id "answer-140301e9-e5d7-5ea2-aa4c-0f869d4dbf85" :answer/id #uuid "140301e9-e5d7-5ea2-aa4c-0f869d4dbf85" :answer/type :answer.type/math :answer/value "-2\pi" :db/ensure [:answer/validate]} {:db/id 17592186097922 :tutorial/content "How can we calculate $\displaystyle{\int} \sin x \cos x \, \textrm{d}x?$  

Notice that we have the product of sine and cosine with the same argument $(x).$ In such cases, we can use the double-angle formula for sine to solve the integral.

Let's recall the double-angle formula for sine, which is

$$
\sin {2x}=2\sin x \cos x.
$$

We can rearrange the above formula as

$$
\sin x \cos x =  \dfrac{1}{2} \sin {2x}.
$$

Plugging this into our integral, we get

$$
\eqalign{
		\int \sin x \cos x \, \textrm{d}x&=\int \dfrac{1}{2}\sin {2x} \, \textrm{d}x\[5pt]
								&=\dfrac{1}{2} \int \sin {2x} \, \textrm{d}x\[5pt]
								&=\dfrac{1}{2} \left( -\dfrac{1}{2} \cos {2x}\right )+C \[5pt]
								&=-\dfrac{1}{4} \cos {2x}+C.	
	}
$$

In general, we can use the double-angle formula for sine to solve any integral that's of the form 

$$
\int \sin\left(ax+b\right)\cos(ax+b)\,\textrm{d}x.
$$

{{field-1}}"] ["question-bfe0bdd7-dbe2-5dd0-8dfa-8c8cabd2a658" :question/worked-solution "The area of the region is given by

$$
A={\int }_{0}^{\pi /4}(4{cos}^{2}⁡(2x)+{sin}^{2}⁡(2x))\,\text{d}x.
$$

Recall  ${cos}^{2}⁡x+{sin}^{2}⁡x=1,$ so we have 

$$
\begin{aligned}4{cos}^{2}⁡(2x)+{sin}^{2}⁡(2x) & =3{cos}^{2}⁡(2x)+({sin}^{2}⁡(2x)+{cos}^{2}⁡(2x)) \\  & =3{cos}^{2}⁡(2x)+1.\end{aligned}
$$

Here, we use the double-angle formula for cosine that involves the ${cos}^{2}⁡x$ term, given by

$$
\operatorname{cos}⁡2x=2{cos}^{2}⁡x-1.
$$

 

Rearranging, we have

$$
2{cos}^{2}⁡x=\operatorname{cos}⁡2x+1.
$$

Hence, the area of the region is

$$
\begin{aligned}A & ={\int }_{0}^{\pi /4}(3{cos}^{2}⁡(2x)+1)\,\text{d}x \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{\pi /4}(\frac{3}{2}\operatorname{cos}⁡4x+\frac{3}{2}+1)\,\text{d}x \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{\pi /4}(\frac{3}{2}\operatorname{cos}⁡4x+\frac{5}{2})\,\text{d}x \\  & ={(\frac{3}{8}\operatorname{sin}⁡4x+\frac{5}{2}x)|}_{0}^{\pi /4} \\  & =[\frac{3}{8}\operatorname{sin}⁡(4\cdot \frac{\pi }{4})+\frac{5}{2}\cdot \frac{\pi }{4}]-[\frac{3}{8}\operatorname{sin}⁡(4\cdot 0)+\frac{5}{2}\cdot 0] \\  & =[\frac{3}{8}\operatorname{sin}⁡(\pi )+\frac{5\pi }{8}]-[\frac{3}{8}\operatorname{sin}⁡(0)+0] \\  & =[\frac{3}{8}\cdot 0+\frac{5\pi }{8}]-[\frac{3}{8}\cdot 0+0] \\  & =\frac{5\pi }{8}.\end{aligned}
$$"] ["question-bfe0bdd7-dbe2-5dd0-8dfa-8c8cabd2a658" :question/difficulty :question.difficulty/hard] ["answer-field-5275b8a3-a8ed-51bd-8426-91952cbec909" :answer-field/id #uuid
